title: Timing is Everything: Inferring Temporal Membership in Continually Updated Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.05781v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Continual model updating has become a common practice in the deployment of machine learning systems. However, the dynamic training behaviors give rise to new risks not sufficiently addressed by existing studies. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated deep learning models. We formalize the notion of temporal membership in continually updated models. We then define the temporal membership inference attack, which seeks to infer whether and when individual samples were involved in model training, at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities. To this end, we propose TMIA, a novel black-box attack that leverages bidirectional LSTMs to infer temporal membership from model outputs observed across successive updates. translated_title: 时机决定一切：推断持续更新模型中的时间成员关系
translated_abstract: 持续模型更新已成为机器学习系统部署中的常见做法。然而，动态训练行为带来了现有研究尚未充分解决的新风险。在本文中，我们首次对持续更新的深度学习模型中的时间隐私风险进行了系统性研究。我们形式化了持续更新模型中“时间成员关系”的概念，并定义了时间成员推断攻击，该攻击旨在在时间戳级别和时间区间级别两种粒度上推断个体样本是否以及何时参与了模型训练。为此，我们提出了TMIA，一种新颖的黑盒攻击方法，它利用双向LSTM从跨连续更新观察到的模型输出中推断时间成员关系。通过在三个语言模型和三个图像分类模型上的大量实验，我们证明TMIA非常有效，并显著优于现有基线方法。
tldr: 本文首次系统研究了持续更新模型中的时间隐私风险，提出了基于双向LSTM的黑盒攻击方法TMIA，能够以时间戳和区间两种粒度推断样本是否以及何时被用于模型训练。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated models, proposing TMIA, a black-box attack based on bidirectional LSTMs that infers whether and when individual samples were involved in training at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities.
